why: Universe 0 for all of A's theorems. A_to_B: (0), (M1), (O1), (O2) come from proposition_16_4_3_supp/_manifold/_orbifold (with definition_16_4_2_manifold/_orbifold to pass from θ to each representative), and (M2) from proposition_16_4_3_naturality_all after identifying B's e, g with suppTransition. B's (O3), the equivalence of the orbifold structures X|supp Θ and X'|supp Θ' of two representatives by a generalized isomorphism compatible with α, α', has no counterpart in A; it was proved outright (lemma o3) by restricting a representative diagram to the supports (EpFunctor.restrictSub, IsEquivalence.restrictSub, theorem_10_3_10), so the two statements differ there only in what is stated, not in what holds. B_to_A: supp, manifold, orbifold, naturality_self and naturality come from B; the transition lemmas, isScSmoothOn_suppTransition and naturality_all were re-proved outright (copied project proofs). The last two say more than B: they cover orbifold-type representatives with arbitrary induced structures, while B's (M2) assumes θ of manifold type.

main.note: Amain → B is not proved at (M2): proposition_16_4_3_naturality gives SOME induced structures PZ, PZ' with sc-diffeomorphic transition, while B asks it for ALL induced structures. Getting there would need the uniqueness of the induced structure (two structures making supp Θ → |supp Θ| a local sc-diffeomorphism agree up to the identity).
